papers.title: Millisecond-scale imaging of fragmented earthquake rupture by near-source fiber-optic sensing
papers.abstract: Small earthquakes [i.e., those of magnitude ( M ) <3] are commonly modeled as simple circular ruptures, leaving the fine-scale spatial attributes of rupture dynamics unresolved. We used near-source distributed acoustic sensing to image the millisecond-scale rupture of an M 2 earthquake within a swarm sequence in California’s Brawley Seismic Zone. Inverting fiber-derived apparent source time functions revealed two distinct rupture episodes separated by 42 milliseconds, reflecting rupture arrest followed by dynamic renucleation. Analysis of a 3-hour sequence showed adjacent, largely nonoverlapping fault patches activated in succession, forming complementary slip partitioning. These fragmented failure patterns within the M 2 rupture and its sequence limited rupture growth, consistent with the absence of a dominant mainshock. Microearthquakes, which are now accessible by fiber-optic sensing, provide direct constraints on fault mechanics across scales bridging laboratory experiments and large earthquakes.

papers.title: Scaling and Cross-Simulation Generalization of Graph Neural Networks for Cosmic-Web Classification in CAMELS
papers.abstract: Graph-based methods can classify galaxies by their dark-matter cosmic-web environments, but reliability beyond development simulations remains uncertain. Galaxy-formation models alter tracer populations and spatial distributions, potentially shifting graph features. We test how graph neural networks scale with independent training realizations and transfer across hydrodynamical simulations. Using the $z=0$ CAMELS IllustrisTNG, SIMBA and Astrid suites, we label galaxies with $M_\star>10^9\,M_\odot$ as void, sheet, filament or knot from the smoothed cold-dark-matter density field. We represent their spatial distributions as periodic Delaunay graphs with ten geometric descriptors. We compare a multilayer perceptron (MLP) and five graph neural networks (GNNs), including a local graph Transformer, under realization-grouped evaluation. Learning curves increase training data from 10 to 100 realizations, with validation and test boxes fixed. We test every source-to-target suite pairing on 100 unseen realizations per target suite. On this external holdout, the Transformer, GAT+ and EdgeConv reach mean per-realization macro-averaged F1 scores of $0.652$, $0.651$ and $0.642$, against $0.481$ for the MLP. The Transformer outperforms the MLP by 0.171, while the difference between the Transformer and GAT+ is not statistically significant. Voids remain the hardest class. Performance is higher in boxes with more selected galaxies and shorter Delaunay edges. Associations with cosmological and feedback parameters weaken after accounting for galaxy richness and void fraction. Our results benchmark the scaling and cross-simulation transfer of galaxy-graph classifiers, demonstrating the value of neighbourhood information and identifying tracer sampling as an important limitation for dark-matter web inference.

papers.title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
papers.abstract: Global warming is expected to accelerate the hydrological cycle, yet its impact on terrestrial water availability is uncertain. Using assimilated streamflow observations from 150 major basins and satellite data for over 1.2 million water bodies, we show a global-scale synchronized decline of streamflow and surface water storage during the 2023–2024 record-warm period, the largest reduction since 1991. South America accounted for 70.4 ± 4.2% of the global streamflow decline. This abrupt depletion was driven by compound ocean–atmosphere forcing, in which concurrent El Niño and tropical North Atlantic warming triggered large-scale atmospheric subsidence, moisture divergence, and amplified drought. These findings reveal that extreme warming can induce abrupt water losses even in humid regions, underscoring a critical vulnerability of global hydrology and water security.

papers.title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 M w 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake
papers.abstract: Rough fault segments typically terminate giant earthquakes but are rarely reported to foster them. However, rupture characteristics of the 2025 moment magnitude ( M w ) 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake are consistent with initiation in a rough zone. Its early rupture was sluggish, lasting ~50 seconds with limited slip but strong, scattered high-frequency radiation. Rupture then propagated southward into a smoother segment, producing >20 meters slip with less intense high-frequency radiation. Using also the rupture characteristics of four M w 7+ foreshocks and aftershocks, we reveal variably sized seismic patches within the rough zone. We interpret these behaviors as manifestations of stress or frictional heterogeneities on the rough segment that favor localized failures yet can foster a giant rupture when spatially connected to a smooth, locked neighboring segment, a scenario previously underrecognized and meriting consideration in seismic hazard assessments.

papers.title: ChemoMAE: Self-Supervised Spectral Representation Learning Reveals Chemical Heterogeneity in Historical Wood
papers.abstract: In historical timber buildings, multiple environmental factors act over centuries on wood whose chemical composition varies across anatomical regions, producing complex patterns of degradation. Understanding how timber members degrade is important for the effective conservation and restoration of historical buildings, yet the mechanisms underlying these patterns remain unclear. To investigate these mechanisms, we used self-supervised learning to establish a common basis for comparing specimens from timber members that differ in wood species and service history. We examined transverse sections of 49 wood specimens from several historical buildings in Japan using near-infrared hyperspectral imaging. ChemoMAE, a self-supervised Transformer, learns pixelwise spectral representations through masked denoising that exploits multicollinearity among spectral variables. Clustering these representations yields spatial maps without predefined chemical-state categories. Because anatomy and degradation can produce spatially continuous regions, we formulated Local Label Agreement (LLA) to quantify agreement among labels assigned to neighboring pixels. Using spectra alone, ChemoMAE yielded higher mean LLA than baseline methods on validation specimens. We then trained ChemoMAE anew and fitted cluster centers across all specimens. Spatial structures consistent with wood anatomy and the expected effects of surface exposure emerged in the resulting maps. By cross-referencing regional spectra and spatial distributions across specimens in light of wood anatomy, service histories, and prior studies, we proposed models of internal and surface degradation as mechanistic hypotheses. This exploratory AI for Science framework gives researchers a basis for linking latent patterns learned through self-supervision with domain knowledge when investigating how material states form.

papers.title: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Adaptive and Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Fully online on-policy distillation (OPD) is costly for long-horizon agents because each update depends on fresh environment rollouts. Prefix replay offers an efficient alternative by sampling current-student responses from stored histories, reducing idle time for long-tail rollouts and allowing each collected trajectory to support multiple updates. However, our analysis of the complete prefix replay pipeline identifies two limitations in long-horizon settings. In trajectory collection, teacher-only trajectories miss student-induced histories, while broader history coverage can reduce teacher reliability. In trajectory reuse, fixed position-based schedules cannot identify critical decisions that may occur at any trajectory depth. We introduce CARE-OPD (Collect for coverAge, Replay with Evidence) to address both limitations. Student-seeded teacher completions and response-level confidence gating expand history coverage while filtering unreliable updates. Hindsight replay allocation then uses downstream execution evidence to select consequential turns. Across long-horizon tasks Software Engineering and Deep Research, CARE-OPD outperforms online OPD and prior prefix replay baselines. On SWE-bench Verified, it raises task success to 59.5% while reducing end-to-end training time by 45% and environment actions by 44% relative to asynchronous online OPD.

papers.title: Counter-ion confinement reverses ion selectivity in subnanometer channels
papers.abstract: Ion transport in nano- and subnanometer channels is central to processes such as ion separation, energy conversion and storage, and nanofluidics. Conventionally, positively charged nanochannels favor anion transport and vice versa. We report that cationic covalent organic framework membranes with sub–one-nanometer channels exhibit selective cation transport. This reversal in selectivity arises from a counter-ion confinement effect, which inverts the electrostatic environment inside the channel wall and creates a secondary confinement region. The counter-ion confinement mechanism concomitantly suppresses coexisting ion competition in mixed-salt systems, enabling membranes to retain high selectivity under practical separation conditions. Our findings provide a design strategy for creating adaptive and highly selective membranes for precise ion transport and separation.
